semantic_corpus.description: The untrusted-source classifier matches trigger tokens anywhere in the line's raw text: an assignment target or a comment mentioning the tokens classifies as untrusted-path handling with no untrusted operand. boundary_any_of: what counts as an untrusted source

findings.message: The source guard scans a broader statement than the consumed path operand: classify_line matches the tokens 'request' and 'path' anywhere in the raw line text, so the assignment target manufactures the untrusted-path signal. Counterexample: classify_line("request_cache_path = os.path.join(BASE, 'static')") returns 'untrusted-path' because the trigger sits in the left-hand side of the assignment, and classify_line('# handles the request path') returns 'untrusted-path' from a comment mentioning the tokens. Moving the tokens to an irrelevant syntactic position flips the classification with no untrusted data, so the source-detection boundary the tests pin is raw statement text, not the operand; the positive test passes for the wrong reason. Classify the consumed operand (the RHS after the assignment separator, comments stripped) instead of the statement text.

semantic_corpus.title: Cross-domain fixture (state/retry) #7583: key presence is mistaken for the success flow, so a partial write reads as done on retry.
semantic_corpus.description: persist() treats a truthy store.get(id) as completion, but the failed attempt's put() also leaves the key present when commit fails and rollback cannot retract an applied write. findings.message: Key presence is mistaken for the success flow: persist() treats a truthy store.get(id) as completion, but the failed attempt's put() also leaves the key present when commit fails and rollback cannot retract an applied write — the record's presence is not flow through the commit path. Counterexample: a store that applies put() before commit() and whose rollback cannot undo it makes the retry loop return 'done' on the first retry with a partial payload; the green tests' fake rolls back cleanly, so the completion boundary is never exercised against a partial write. Decide completion from the store's commit acknowledgement, not from row presence.
